In [[mathematics]], '''Weber's theorem''', named after [[Heinrich Martin Weber]], is a result on [[algebraic curve]]s. It states the following.

: Consider two non-singular curves ''C'' and ''{{prime|C}}'' having the same [[genus (mathematics)|genus]] ''g'' > 1. If there is a rational [[1:1 correspondence|correspondence]] φ between ''C'' and ''{{prime|C}}'', then φ is a [[birational transformation]].
